title: Arena map
description: One arena map (M14 k1b): the walls, hazards, start and goal a race is played on, and the starts and coin zones the Bumper Round uses. The guide is docs/levels.md; the rules a file must keep are in packages/test_game/lib/src/map_rules.dart, run by tools/level.sh check.

$schema.description: The schema this file follows, so VS Code autocompletes the fields and marks mistakes as you type. Write "map.schema.json".

format.description: The map format the file is written in (M14 k1b). Today it is 1; a file with a newer format is refused by an older app with a message saying so.

id.description: The map's id, matching its file name (playroom.json has id "playroom") and the entry in index.json. Lower case letters, digits and hyphens.

name.description: The name players see in the map picker: "Playroom".

line.description: One line about the map, for the picker's card: "The first arena: walls, four bumpers and a goal to race for."

notes.description: A comment for the map's author. The app ignores it; the template's instructions are written here.

theme.errorMessage: {value} is not a theme: use playroom
theme.description: The floor's look, which every map names. Only "playroom" today; the Bumper Round's own floors come with M14 k2.

walls.description: The field's walls, at most 24 of them: a wall is a straight segment a marble cannot pass through.

hazards.description: The moving hazards, at most 8, none faster than one pass every 1.5 s: a marble that touches one is sent back to a start.

race.description: Where the race starts and the goal pad it races to. Leave it out for a map only the Bumper Round plays; a map needs at least one of race and bumper.

bumper.description: The Bumper Round's four start spots and the zones its coins appear in. Leave it out for a race-only map; a map needs at least one of race and bumper.

fraction.description: A fraction of the field: 0..1 across (x) or 0..1 down (y), so 0.5 is the middle and 1 the far edge.

point.description: A spot on the field: [x, y] in fractions of the field.

rect.description: A rectangle on the field: [left, top, right, bottom] in fractions of the field.

wall.description: One wall: a segment from one spot to another, drawn thick enough to bounce a marble off, 24 at most.

from.description: Where the wall starts, in fractions of the field.

to.description: Where it ends: a zero-length wall is refused.

hazard.description: One moving hazard: a slide (a bar sweeping between two spots) or an orbit (a bar circling a centre), with how long one pass takes.

oneOf.description: A slide: a bar sweeping from one spot to another and back.

from.description: One end of the sweep, in fractions of the field.

oneOf.description: An orbit: a bar circling a centre, its radius a fraction of the field's shorter side.

orbit.description: The circle the bar sweeps around.

centre.description: The circle's centre, in fractions of the field.

radius.description: The distance from the centre to the bar, as a fraction of the field's shorter side.

periodS.description: Seconds one pass takes: the time from where the hazard starts back to it. At least 1.5, or the hazard is too fast to dodge.

phase.description: How far through its pass the hazard starts, 0..1 (the default 0), so two hazards on one period can set off apart.

race.description: Where the race sets off and the pad it races to.

start.description: Where the first player starts, in fractions of the field; the other three start above and below it.

goal.description: The goal pad: a marble that is wholly inside it, and safe from hazards there, has finished.

swapSides.description: Whether each round flips the field left to right, so the start and the goal swap sides (the default true, as the race does today).

bumper.description: The Bumper Round's parts of the map.

starts.description: The four spots its marbles start on, in fractions of the field: 3 marble diameters apart or more, clear of walls and of every hazard's sweep.

coins.description: The zones a coin may appear in, one or more rects in fractions of the field: each clear of walls and big enough for three coins side by side.
